question: How has our view on ASML changed since Q1 2026?
reference_answer: In January 2026 ASML was Hold with a EUR 880 PT on China export curbs. In April it was upgraded to Buy with PT EUR 1,050 after Q1 orders of EUR 7.1bn and broader High-NA adoption. In July the PT rose to EUR 1,120 after a Q2 beat; in September Buy and EUR 1,120 were kept despite a possible High-NA delay at TSMC A14.

question: What was our rating on Novo Nordisk before the March 2026 downgrade, and why did we downgrade?
reference_answer: Novo was Buy (DKK 520 PT) before being downgraded to Hold with a DKK 400 PT on 19 March 2026, because of deeper US net price cuts under the MFN agreement, persistent compounded semaglutide, and underwhelming CagriSema REDEFINE 4 data versus tirzepatide.

question: What is our current price target on TSMC?
reference_answer: USD 300 (set 17 July 2026), rated Buy.

question: Why did we downgrade SAP?
reference_answer: SAP was downgraded to Hold from Buy in April 2026 (PT cut to EUR 250 from EUR 300) because current cloud backlog growth slowed to 22% from 27% and US public sector deals slipped, breaking the thesis that backlog growth would stay above 25%.

question: Which stocks were removed from or added to our top picks list at mid-year?
reference_answer: At mid-year SAP was removed from the top picks after its April downgrade and ASML was added after its upgrade to Buy.

question: What CoWoS capacity do we expect TSMC to reach by the end of 2026?
reference_answer: About 110k wafers per month by end-2026, up from roughly 75k at end-2025.

question: What did we say about BP's gearing in August 2026?
reference_answer: Gearing fell to 21% after the USD 10bn Castrol sale closed, which drove the upgrade to Hold.

question: What are the key risks we flag in our HSBC coverage?
reference_answer: Hong Kong commercial real estate stress, lower HIBOR compressing NII, and China growth.

question: Summarise our views on European banks.
reference_answer: European bank NII has been more resilient to rate cuts than feared thanks to structural hedges; capital return yields of 8-10% are attractive and we prefer banks with excess capital and hedge tailwinds such as HSBC (Buy).

question: What Brent assumption underpins our Shell estimates after May 2026?
reference_answer: USD 65/bbl, cut from USD 72 in May 2026.

question: When did we upgrade AMD, and what was the catalyst?
reference_answer: AMD was upgraded to Buy from Hold on 5 August 2026 (PT USD 240 from 200) on the start of MI450 Helios rack-scale shipments and H2 data center GPU guidance above USD 6bn.

question: What was NVIDIA's fiscal Q4 data center revenue?
reference_answer: USD 62bn.

question: Which stocks have we rated Sell in 2026, and are any still Sell?
reference_answer: BP was rated Sell in February and May 2026; it was upgraded to Hold in August, so none is currently rated Sell.

question: How did LVMH's organic growth trend through the first half of 2026?
reference_answer: Fashion & Leather was -3% organic in Q4 2025, group organic sales were -2% in Q1 2026, and Fashion & Leather returned to +1% in Q2 2026, prompting an upgrade to Buy.

question: What is our price target for AstraZeneca and how is it derived?
reference_answer: 16,500p, from a sum-of-the-parts DCF assuming an 8% revenue CAGR to 2030 and a 7.5% WACC.

question: Compare our ratings on ASML and TSMC in April 2026.
reference_answer: Both were Buy in April 2026: ASML was upgraded to Buy with a EUR 1,050 PT, TSMC was Buy with PT raised to USD 285.

question: What did our obesity market note say about price erosion?
reference_answer: We model US GLP-1 net prices falling 35-45% by 2030 as volumes expand; the market still reaches USD 120bn by 2030 but incumbents lose share.

question: What happened to Microsoft's Azure growth between January and April 2026?
reference_answer: Azure growth eased slightly from 38% to 37% in constant currency.

question: What is our view on AI capex in the second half of 2026?
reference_answer: No sign of a slowdown: top four hyperscalers on track for about USD 520bn of 2026 capex and roughly 30% growth in 2027; power and packaging are the constraints.

question: Did we change our JPMorgan rating at any point in 2026?
reference_answer: No. JPMorgan stayed Hold all year while the PT rose from USD 310 to 315 to 320.

question: How large were ASML's Q1 2026 net bookings?
reference_answer: EUR 7.1bn, against consensus of EUR 5.4bn.

question: What did our field check say about High-NA insertion at TSMC's A14 node?
reference_answer: Checks suggest TSMC will not insert High-NA at A14 until 2028; we trimmed 2027 High-NA units from 14 to 11 but kept ASML at Buy.

question: What drove the BP upgrade?
reference_answer: Closing of the USD 10bn Castrol sale and gearing falling to 21%, easing balance-sheet concerns; Elliott keeps capital discipline in focus.

question: How much is Shell buying back per quarter after Q1 2026 results?
reference_answer: USD 3.0bn per quarter, trimmed from USD 3.5bn.

question: Summarise our software sector view on seat-based pricing.
reference_answer: AI agents threaten seat-based pricing; consumption or outcome-based vendors are better placed, and we expect a shift to hybrid seat-plus-consumption models through 2027.

question: Who covers Novo Nordisk and what is the latest price target?
reference_answer: Hannah Lindqvist; latest PT DKK 360 (Hold), set 10 September 2026.

question: What did we say about SAP's cloud backlog in July 2026?
reference_answer: Current cloud backlog growth slowed again to 21% despite Business Data Cloud traction; Hold, PT EUR 245.

question: Can the oil majors sustain their buybacks at USD 65 Brent?
reference_answer: Shell can sustain about USD 3bn a quarter from free cash flow; BP cannot fund more than USD 0.75bn without raising gearing.

question: What were our top picks at the start of 2026?
reference_answer: TSMC, NVIDIA, Microsoft, SAP, HSBC and AstraZeneca.

question: What did we say about luxury demand in China in September 2026?
reference_answer: Mainland China luxury spending stabilised in July-August and Hainan duty-free sales rose for the first time in eight quarters, an early recovery signal supporting the LVMH Buy.
